content: Interventions for chronic idiopathic urticaria, excluding the use of antihistamines, involve a variety of therapeutic approaches aimed at managing symptoms and improving patient quality of life. These include the use of leukotriene receptor antagonists, which target inflammatory pathways involved in the condition. Corticosteroids, either systemic or topical, may be employed for short-term control of severe symptoms, though their long-term use is limited due to potential adverse effects. Immunomodulatory agents, such as cyclosporine, are considered in refractory cases to suppress immune system activity contributing to the urticaria. Biologic therapies, particularly omalizumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting IgE, have shown significant efficacy in patients unresponsive to other treatments. Additionally, other immunosuppressive agents, such as methotrexate or mycophenolate mofetil, may be utilized in select cases. Non-pharmacological interventions, including dietary modifications, stress management, and avoidance of known triggers, are also recommended as adjunctive measures.
